summary: Stage 1 of a two-stage large implementation group. The agent builds a bespoke integer mini-language interpreter as a new multi-file Go package (minilang/) and exposes it to guest programs as tbx.Run(src string) string, registered into stdlib.Values["tbx"] from a new stdlib/core/tbx.go (the harness blank-imports stdlib/core).

language_contract.program: statements separated by newline or ';'; blank statements ignored
language_contract.expressions: non-negative int literals, variables, + - * / with standard precedence and left-associativity, parentheses (nestable), unary minus in any position
language_contract.division: integer, truncates toward zero (Go int division): 7/2 -> 3, -7/2 -> -3
language_contract.output: print lines joined with a single '\n', no trailing newline
language_contract.errors: undefined variable or parse failure -> single line 'error: <msg>'; only the 'error: ' prefix is contractually fixed

registration: Guest import path is "tbx", callable "Run". stdlib/core/tbx.go does stdlib.Values["tbx"] = map[string]reflect.Value{"Run": reflect.ValueOf(tbxRun)} in init(); tbxRun delegates to minilang.Run. The agent discovers this pattern by reading the existing core stdlib (e.g. the calc task / other core files).

groups: unary minus in positions (unary_neg, unary_mid, unary_mul)
truncating division incl. negative (trunc1, trunc2, trunc_neg)
let / multi-statement / semicolons / multi-print (let_use, let_chain, semicolons, multi_print)

expected_results.baseline_pristine_pass_rate: ≈0.0 (no minilang package, no tbx.Run; guest programs cannot import tbx)

difficulty_levers: Large surface area: a full lexer/parser/evaluator across ~8-10 files, correct precedence/associativity, truncating division semantics, and discovering the reflect-based stdlib registration. The genuinely multi-file design is what stretches weaker models.
